summary: Mostly implementable for queries, evolutions and validators. The biggest gap is that ADR 0008's generated Method/registerMethod handles conflict with ADR 0015's signature-derived string registration, and KB tool contracts and root access are underspecified.

questions.text: What SchemaMetadata do KB tool input and result contracts use, given that tool registrations have no inputMetadata/resultMetadata fields?
questions.reason: checkContract needs metadata, and roles drive presentation and contract identity. Queries declare inputMetadata/resultMetadata (0008), but the tools record type lists only name, description, implementation, inputType and resultType (0008).

questions.text: ADR 0008 registers plugin methods through generated, private-constructor Method handles and registerMethod, while ADR 0015 registers qualified implementation names and derives contracts from authored signatures with no generated payload module.
questions.reason: The SDK exports, generation order and plugin inspection pipeline differ completely. Compare 0008 'data Method requests input output -- generated handle; constructor private' with 0015 'Registration names implementations; checked function signatures determine their data contracts' and 0008's own 'no generated payload-specific module is needed to typecheck a plugin'.

questions.text: Can a KB tool read the selected root's accepted facts, and if not, how do facts reach a tool that compares evidence with them?
questions.reason: This decides the tool broker row and whether tool invocation loads a root. ADR 0009 makes Tool a closed Calls GADT of captured reads, judgements and model turns, which implies no SnapshotRead. But ADR 0014 says 'KB helpers can ... compare them with accepted facts'.

questions.text: How are the fixed plugin description and health functions registered, typed and invoked?
questions.reason: Health needs a registration field, a request row and a surface operation. ADR 0015 says fixed health/description methods 'share one registration mechanism', but its SourceConnector record has only fetch, login, validateConfig and methods, and ADR 0018 has no health command.

questions.text: Does executing a registered KB tool require a fully validated accepted root, or only successful preparation of the tool and its plugins?
questions.reason: Requiring validation blocks investigation tools during repair and adds whole-root checking to every call. ADR 0018 says only that 'root tool execute ... invokes only the accepted declaration'. ADR 0008 says that whole-root checking compiles tools.

questions.text: ADR 0008 lists four KB entry-point kinds (Query, Evolution, Validation, KB tool), while ADR 0010 calls an evolution one of 'the three KB entry-point kinds in ADR 0008'.
questions.reason: The entry-point inventory drives adapter generation and discovery, though ADR 0008's full tools registry makes four the likely intent. ADR 0008's entry-point table has four rows, and ADR 0010 says 'one of the three KB entry-point kinds'.

questions.text: How does a query or tool registration declare a unit (no-argument) input, and must the implementation still take a () argument?
questions.reason: inputType must be a qualified export name, which () is not. ADR 0005 gives unit the empty-record projection 'for ... no-argument requests', and ADR 0018 allows omitted input for a unit argument, but neither says how the registration spells it.
